title: Vancouver Road Safety Analytics
label: GEOSPATIAL DATA ANALYTICS
summary: An interactive Vancouver road-safety dashboard integrating 2.47M parking tickets with ICBC collision data and geographic quality checks.
overview: An end-to-end geospatial analytics project connecting City of Vancouver parking violations (2020–2025), the municipal road network, and ICBC collision data (2021–2025). The workflow standardizes source records, performs approximate geographic matching, audits data quality, and presents road-level patterns through a published interactive dashboard.

sections.title: Research question
sections.text: How do parking enforcement patterns, changes across years, and approximate collision locations vary across Vancouver roads? The goal is exploratory understanding, not a causal or exposure-adjusted road safety ranking.

sections.title: Data engineering and geographic matching
items: Normalize street and block identifiers across 2,472,917 input parking-ticket records.
Use official road geometry for street-range matching and approximate ICBC collision location assignment.
Audit accepted, excluded, unmatched and ambiguous records before generating analysis-ready tables.

sections.title: Dashboard and interaction
items: Explore parking, collision and comparison analysis layers with multi-year filters.
Inspect highlighted road segments, infraction types and road-level change.
Select a location and radius to examine nearby collision counts, severity and involvement categories.

sections.title: Validation and limits
sections.text: A local end-to-end rebuild passed 37 checks with zero failures, one CDN-related warning and one browser-interactivity check skipped by static QA. Raw ticket and collision counts are not normalized by traffic, parking exposure or enforcement intensity; geographic matches are approximate.

contribution: Built Python data cleaning and geographic matching for the original group parking analysis and implemented its interactive Folium map. The later ICBC integration and v12-series dashboard are subsequent extensions; the project documentation distinguishes the academic team contribution from later development.

title: Home Affordability Calculator
label: HOUSING & DECISIONS
summary: Spreadsheet-based housing affordability and rent-versus-buy analysis, with an interactive calculator planned.
overview: A housing affordability and rent-versus-buy assignment built in a spreadsheet. It considers mortgage payments, debt, savings and housing costs as inputs to a financial decision. The next stage is a planned rebuild into an interactive calculator; a finished web application is not yet available.

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: Housing decisions involve several connected financial commitments. This assignment examines affordability alongside the comparison between renting and buying, keeping mortgage payments, existing debt, savings and housing costs in the same decision framework.

sections.title: What the spreadsheet covers
items: Mortgage payments as a recurring housing commitment.
Debt and savings as part of the affordability picture.
Housing costs in the rent-versus-buy comparison.
Spreadsheet analysis as a way to organize assumptions and examine financial decisions.

sections.title: Planned interactive rebuild
sections.text: The proposed rebuild would turn the spreadsheet’s decision framework into a calculator with explicit inputs and readable outputs. The interface, calculations and assumptions still need to be specified and validated before a working demo can be presented.
items: Define the input fields and explain how each affects the comparison.
Organize outputs around affordability and rent-versus-buy questions.
Make assumptions visible so scenarios can be compared consistently.
Check the rebuilt calculations against the spreadsheet before publishing results.

sections.title: Current status and limitations
sections.text: The existing work is a spreadsheet assignment. The interactive experience, final validation results and public demo remain planned. No current affordability recommendation or verified calculator output is presented here.

title: U.S. Treasury Yield Analysis
label: YIELDS & FORECASTS
summary: Analysis of U.S. 10-year Treasury yields across recession periods using ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting in R.
overview: A time-series project analyzing U.S. 10-year Treasury yields across recession periods and using ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting. The project combines statistical modeling in R with economic interpretation and forecast evaluation.

sections.title: Analysis question
sections.text: The project examines how the yield series behaves across recession periods and how time-series models can be used to forecast it. The emphasis is on describing the series, modeling its temporal structure and interpreting forecasts in an economic context.

sections.title: Methods and tools
items: R for the time-series analysis and modeling workflow.
U.S. 10-year Treasury yields as the series under study.
Recession periods as context for examining historical behavior.
ARIMA and SARIMA as forecasting approaches.
Forecast evaluation and economic interpretation as parts of the analysis.

sections.title: Model comparison

sections.title: Interpretation and limitations
sections.text: This is an academic analysis of a historical yield series. Forecasts depend on the model specification and evaluation period. The project is not presented as a current interest-rate outlook or financial recommendation.

title: WTI Crude Oil Market Model
label: EXPLORATORY MARKET MODEL
summary: Exploratory WTI analysis alongside VIX, trading volume and shipping indicators, using Lotka–Volterra-inspired modeling and Bollinger Bands.
overview: An academic modeling project exploring WTI crude oil prices alongside VIX, trading volume and shipping indicators. It uses Lotka–Volterra-inspired modeling and Bollinger Bands as exploratory ways to examine market behavior.

sections.title: Research scope
sections.text: The project considers WTI prices in a wider market setting by examining volatility, trading activity and shipping indicators alongside the price series. These inputs provide an exploratory framework for studying patterns rather than establishing a causal explanation.

sections.title: Modeling approach
items: WTI prices as the central market series.
VIX, trading volume and shipping indicators as additional series explored alongside WTI.
Lotka–Volterra-inspired modeling to explore interacting market dynamics.
Bollinger Bands as an additional lens for examining price behavior.

sections.title: Validation space
sections.text: A dedicated area is reserved for model validation, fit diagnostics and sensitivity checks. Final validation results have not been provided for this portfolio page, so the model is not described as validated or as outperforming a benchmark.

sections.title: Limitations
items: Patterns between market series do not by themselves establish causality.
An exploratory model does not demonstrate profitable trading performance.
Results depend on model assumptions and the data window; those details still need to be documented.
The project does not present a live trading strategy or current oil-price recommendation.

sections.title: Next development step
sections.text: The next version can document model assumptions, add validation evidence and present the limitations beside the results. The goal is to make the reasoning and uncertainty inspectable before drawing stronger conclusions.
